text:
incident-bot: Incident created: [INC-2026-042] KV-cache paged blowup & continous-batching perf cliff. Priority: P1. Trigger: rapid increase in 429/latency from 4 customers in us-west-2.

maya: seeing a lot of spikes on the 99th and steady rise in blockmanager memory usage. paging rate up 8x last 15m.

alex: +1. graphs show batch queue length jumped after the `batch_threshold_ms` rollback we pushed at 03:12 UTC. suspect continuous batching change allowed huge prefixes to accumulate.

jon: confirm: logs show repeated `kv_block_alloc` followed by `block_meta_append` twice per block — looks like metadata not being compacted. possible leak. snippet:```
[EPOCH 1819876521] alloc block_id=0x7f3b12 size=1.2MB
[EPOCH 1819876522] meta_attach block_id=0x7f3b12 owner=shard-9
[EPOCH 1819876523] meta_attach block_id=0x7f3b12 owner=shard-9
```

maya: customers A and D reported 5-10s tail latencies + some 429s. SLO impact: borderline for paid tiers. notifying CS.

ops-lead: can we mitigate without full rollback? thinking: tighten batch thresholds, increase eviction aggressiveness, and temporarily scale dedicated pools.

alex: i can roll the batch threshold back to conservative value (from 100ms to 20ms) and flip on early eviction for paged KV (eviction_factor=1.5 -> 1.1). rolling hotfix now in canary.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: redwood/serving:kv-evict-hotfix sha=deadbeef -> canary shard=us-west-2a.

jon: also found a rare code path where block metadata refcount isn't decremented when `batch_cancel` fires. quick patch ready; needs build+smoke. i can push to canary after the threshold change to verify reduced pressure.

maya: customer-impact update: CS pinged customers: they see elevated latency and intermittent rate limit errors. Ticket numbers: CS-4532, CS-4534, CS-4537.

alex: canary results (10m): request rate normalized, paging events down 60%, tail latency improving ~40% for canary shards. no error spike on the canary.

jon: ok i'll cut the metadata refcount patch into `kv-fix/patch-127` and request a canary build. smoke tests include: `make smoke-alloc`, `make smoke-evict`.

maya: important: we can't full rollback the last runtime because it had other bug fixes. prefer targeted config and the metadata patch. ops-lead, if canary stays green, plan to rollout to remaining shards in 20m windows.

ops-lead: agreed. coordinate with infra to pre-warm eviction threads and bump cache GC interval to 30s during rollout to reduce churning. notify billing/alerts so we don't get paged again for expected transient metrics.

deploy-bot: canary deploy completed ok: redwood/serving:kv-evict-hotfix sha=deadbeef -> us-west-2a status=success.

alex: starting staged rollout to us-west-2b/c with 15m pause windows. commands used:```
# tighten batch threshold
curl -X POST https://admin-api.internal/configs -d '{"batch_threshold_ms":20}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
# set eviction factor
curl -X POST https://admin-api.internal/configs -d '{"eviction_factor":1.1}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

jon: canary logs show no duplicate meta_attach after patch. run for 30m before final decision. also added assert in debug build to catch refcount drift.

maya: monitoring: paging events and block allocations trending down. latency heading back near baseline. still ~2 customers with intermittent 429s but CS says they're ok with status updates.

ops-lead: after we finish rollout, schedule a full postmortem and a follow-up task to add an automated regression test for the batch threshold + paged-KV interaction.

alex: rollout finished across us-west-2. all shards show normalized paging rates. starting gradual revert of temporary GC bump after 30m.

jon: patch queued for merge to main; will include better refcount unit tests and a small changelog entry about the edge-case. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/kv/+/4567

maya: customer impact summary for postmortem: 4 customers affected, elevated tail latencies for ~45m, intermittent 429s for 20m during peak. mitigations: config tightening, eviction tuning, metadata refcount patch. no data loss.

ops-lead: handing off to next oncall for follow-ups and postmortem writeup. @sarah you're up for the 08:00 UTC shift — please validate the post-rollout metrics and start the blameless postmortem doc. key owners: alex (config rollout), jon (metadata patch), maya (customer comms).

sarah: ack. i'll validate graphs, check for regressions, and kick off the PM doc. will reach out if anything spikes. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity->resolved; duration 00:52:57. Resolution summary: config hotfix + code patch mitigated paging and metadata leak. Postmortem owners assigned.

maya: leaving a short runbook note: if paging rate > 3x baseline after threshold changes -> set `batch_threshold_ms=10`, `eviction_factor=1.0`, and escalate to eng-runtime oncall.

sarah: noted. closing thread and collecting logs for the postmortem.
